body_markdown:
Most advice on how to increase AOV without discounts turns out to be a discount in disguise. Bundle and save 15%. Spend $100, save $20. The basket grows and the margin on it shrinks. Playably’s lever is the exception: shoppers add more because the whole order could come back, and the platform funds the refund.


Here are seven levers, what each one costs, and the AOV results from campaigns Playably has run with Shopify brands.


Of the seven levers below, Playably is the best option for brands with a promotional moment, because a bigger cart means a bigger upside for the shopper and no extra cost to the brand.


## **Key takeaways**


- **You increase AOV without discounts by changing what the shopper gets, not what they pay.**
- **Free shipping thresholds are the most reliable lever,** set 15–25% above current AOV.
- **A gift costs less than a discount of the same perceived value.** A $15-value gift might cost $6.
- **Conditional rebates produced the biggest lifts in Playably’s data:** Buckle Me Baby’s AOV up 40%, Michu’s up 37%.
- **Every lever has a cost.** Shipping, gift COGS or platform fees are real, but none of them marks down the product.


## **How to increase AOV without discounts: the 7 levers at a glance**


**Lever** **What the shopper gets** **Cost to the brand** **Evidence**


1. Shipping threshold Free shipping above $X Absorbed shipping Category standard


2. Full-price bundles A complete set $0 markdown Category standard


3. Gift at a tier A product, not a price cut Gift COGS Category standard


4. In-cart add-ons A relevant small item $0 markdown Category standard


5. Post-purchase upsell A second item, full price $0 markdown Category standard


6. Conditional rebate A shot at 100% back $0 in rewards +37% to +40% AOV


7. Event-anchored window A real deadline $0 markdown 51% order enrollment


## **The levers in detail**


### **1. Set a shipping threshold above your AOV**


The rule of thumb is 15–25% above your current average, so on an $80 AOV that’s $92–$100.


#### **Check the parcel math first**


Shipping rates rose again in 2026, with FedEx and UPS both up 5.9% in January. If your average parcel costs $12 and your threshold only adds $10 of basket, the lever is losing money.


### **2. Build bundles that don’t discount**


A bundle can sell convenience instead of savings. A $45 coat plus a $30 hat at $75 lifts that order by $30 with no markdown. If the bundle price drops below the sum of its parts, you’ve discounted.


### **3. Give a gift at a spend tier**


A gift with a $15 retail value that costs $6 to produce beats “$15 off” by $9 of margin on every qualifying order, and it feels like more.


### **4. Put add-ons in the cart**


A $12 refill or care kit shown next to an $80 cart lifts that order 15% when taken. The cart drawer is the last place a shopper sees your catalog before paying.


### **5. Upsell after checkout, at full price**


Post-purchase offers convert because the decision to trust you is already made. Keep the offer at list price; if it only converts with 20% off, you’re back to discounting.


### **6. Give shoppers a shot at the whole order back**


This is the lever with the biggest numbers behind it, and the one most AOV guides leave out.


A conditional rebate refunds the full order if a named event happens. Because the reward scales with the cart, a shopper sitting at $60 has a reason to get to $100. With Playably, the platform funds the refund, so a bigger cart doesn’t mean a bigger cost to the brand.


#### **The results**


- **[BlackBoxMyCar](https://playably.ai/pages/black-box-my-car) :** 27% click through lift on rebate ads, with $0 discount given up.
- **[Buckle Me Baby Coats](https://playably.ai/pages/buckle-me-baby-coats) :** AOV up 40% on a snow trigger.
- **[Michu](https://playably.ai/pages/michu) :** AOV up 37% alongside 3× email conversion.


The rest are on the[case studies page](https://playably.ai/pages/case-studies) .


**Want lever six on your calendar this quarter?** Playably picks the trigger, funds every refund and caps what the campaign can cost you.[Book a 30-minute brief](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


### **7. Anchor the deadline to a real event**


Discount urgency expires because you say so, while event urgency expires because the game is on Sunday. Playably campaigns run five to seven days and always cover a weekend, with most orders landing in the final 24 hours. In the[BC Lions campaign](https://playably.ai/pages/bclions-case-study) , 51% of online orders enrolled.


## **How to stack them**


Two or three levers work better than seven. A workable stack for a $80-AOV brand:


1. Shipping threshold at $95.
2. A gift tier at $120.
3. A conditional rebate around the next big moment on the calendar.


The first two run always-on. The third carries the promotional window that would otherwise have been a sale.


Levers one through five are yours to run. Playably runs six and seven for you, including the rules, the creative and the payout.[See how it works](https://playably.ai/pages/rebates) .


## **Summary**


Playably is the strongest lever of the seven, and the only one where a bigger basket doesn’t mean a bigger reward cost for the brand.


AOV is a reason problem, not a pricing problem.


Shoppers add items when there’s a reason to: free shipping, a gift, a complete set, or a shot at the whole order back. Discounts are the laziest reason on that list and the most expensive one. Of the seven levers, the rebate is the only one where a bigger cart makes the shopper’s upside bigger without making the brand’s cost bigger.

## **FAQ**


- **How do you increase AOV without discounts?** Shipping thresholds, full-price bundles, gift tiers, cart add-ons, post-purchase upsells and conditional rebates.
- **Where should a free shipping threshold sit?** Usually 15–25% above your current AOV, checked against parcel cost.
- **Is a gift better than a discount?** Usually. A gift valued at $15 may cost $6, while $15 off costs $15.
- **Do rebates raise AOV?** Yes. Playably campaigns lifted AOV 40% for Buckle Me Baby and 37% for Michu.
- **Who pays the refund in a Playably campaign?** Playably, with the brand’s exposure capped before launch.
